searchText: Yes, it did lower it, but it was not unintentionally <@905058765022310460> The EIP seems to motivate the slashing parameter adjustment by the [following](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7251#making-the-initial-slashing-penalty-negligible): "To encourage consolidation, we could modify the slashing penalties". Given that everything is still linear, I don't see how the EIP achieves its goal. Just my .02$. I just discovered that there is a lengthy discussion on ethresear.ch. I'll look there. Also consider that this is just the initial slashing penalty, there are 2 more potential penalties. In a mass slashing event, like it happend on Holesky a few weeks ago, a validator still loses all there ETH. https://eth2book.info/capella/part2/incentives/slashing/ <@905058765022310460> Thanks, I was just trying to get to a worst case scenario for the math inside `process_slashings`. My worst case calculation for mainnet is that 24.5 ETH out of 32 ETH are lost. Not all of the stake. Not my expertise, but for example on Holesky the exit queue is more than 1 year long. While validators are in the queue the still get attestation penalties. So I think it depends how long the queue is <@905058765022310460> You are right. Thanks, I misread a few functions in the spec. <@905058765022310460> On your Holesky exit queue remark: Why is there the additional penalty for slashed validators to suffer on their way out? [`get_attestation_component_deltas`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#helpers) has: ``` for index in get_eligible_validator_indices(state): if index in unslashed_attesting_indices: # .... else: penalties[index] += get_base_reward(state, index) ``` So slashed validators just get a penalty no matter what they do, right? Even if they vote correctly, they get the penalty applied. How much that is cummulatively depends on how full the exit queue is. Isn't that a bit random? We already have correlation penalties implemented in `process_slashings`. Let's assume that you end up on the minority chain, and that you attested correctly. Your goal is to burn as much ETH on the majority side as possible. One strategy would be to do a voluntary exit with your validators, such that you clog up the exit queue and amplify the pain when majority validator switch over to the minority chain. Once you're slashed you don't get any duties assigned to you though, so there's no penalties for missing duties you haven't been assigned (Afaik) You are still assigned duties (you're still active until you exit, and all active validators are assigned duties), but your attestations don't count so yes you are punished for it. And yes it's a bit of an odd system. ahh you're right, you get the duties but it doesnt count!

<@905058765022310460> On your Holesky exit queue remark: Why is there the additional penalty for slashed validators to suffer on their way out? [`get_attestation_component_deltas`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#helpers) has:
```
    for index in get_eligible_validator_indices(state):
        if index in unslashed_attesting_indices:
            # ....
        else:
            penalties[index] += get_base_reward(state, index)
```
So slashed validators just get a penalty no matter what they do, right? Even if they vote correctly, they get the penalty applied. How much that is cummulatively depends on how full the exit queue is. Isn't that a bit random? We already have correlation penalties implemented in `process_slashings`.
